PROBLEM: the script raises staging's FREYTAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE through the Railway CLI (`variable set`, which restarts the container), then sleeps 60 s and polls only /api/v1/health. GitHub Actions reports a deploy finished before Railway has swapped containers, and while a redeploy is in flight the OLD container still answers /health, so a run can start against a restarting container. Railway itself knows the deployment state, so ask Railway instead of polling the app.

FACTS (verified against the real CLI): `npx --yes @railway/cli@latest deployment list --project P --service S --environment E --limit 3 --json` prints a JSON array, newest first, of objects with `id`, `status` (values seen: SUCCESS, REMOVED; in flight values are INITIALIZING, BUILDING, DEPLOYING; bad ones are FAILED and CRASHED), `createdAt`, and `meta` (an object that may or may not have `commitHash`; deployments triggered by a variable change keep the same code and may lack it). The service has a healthcheck configured in railway.toml, so SUCCESS means the new container passed its healthcheck. The script already defines `rw=(npx --yes @railway/cli@latest)` and `scope=(--project ... --service ... --environment ...)`; use them.

DO: add two functions and use them.
1. `latest_deployment_id`: runs the list command with --limit 1 --json and prints the newest deployment's id (sort by createdAt descending in python3 to be safe; print nothing if the list is empty or the CLI fails).
2. `wait_for_new_deployment <previous_id> [timeout_seconds=600]`: poll every WAIT_POLL_SECONDS (default 10; 0 means no sleep) until the newest deployment's id differs from previous_id AND its status is SUCCESS. If the newest differing deployment is FAILED or CRASHED print a FAIL line containing the word FAILED or CRASHED with its id and status and return 1. If the timeout passes (WAIT_GIVEUP_SECONDS overrides 600) print FAIL with the last id and status seen and return 1. On success make ONE confirmation request `curl -sf --max-time 15 "$E2E_API_BASE_URL/api/v1/version"` and require channel "staging" and runtime "scene-v1"; if env EXPECTED_SHA is set also require sha == EXPECTED_SHA; a failed confirmation retries up to 6 times 5 s apart (no sleep when WAIT_POLL_SECONDS=0), then returns 1. Print one line per poll with the status seen.
USE: in the main flow, record `prev=$(latest_deployment_id)` immediately BEFORE `variable set`, and replace the `sleep 60` plus the health loop by `wait_for_new_deployment "$prev"` (FAIL and exit 1 if it returns non-zero). In `restore`: record the id before the variable delete; after the delete, if a NEWER deployment appears within 30 s (poll with the same interval) call `wait_for_new_deployment` for it, best effort: a failure only prints a WARNING and never changes the exit status; if none appears in 30 s print that no redeploy was triggered and continue (the existing code deletes with --skip-deploys first, which may not redeploy). Keep set -u, the trap, and every other behaviour, including the replicate and merge logic, unchanged. Use only bash, curl, npx and python3 (python3 -c for JSON; no jq).
TESTABILITY: if env WAIT_FOR_RAILWAY_SELFTEST=1 the script defines the functions, then runs ONLY a self-test hook and exits with its status BEFORE reading .env, touching Railway, or doing anything else: the hook sets `prev=$(latest_deployment_id)`, calls `wait_for_new_deployment "$prev"`, and exits with that status. The check puts a fake `npx` and a fake `curl` first in PATH; the fake npx ignores its arguments and the script is run as `bash scene-affordance-l2-all-live.sh 1`. In the self-test, scope and rw may be unset-safe: define rw and scope BEFORE the hook with placeholder values if the real ones need .env (for example scope=(--project p --service s --environment e)). Put the hook right after the function definitions and argument parsing, so none of the existing top-of-script lines (cd, .env sourcing, case on replicate count) need to run first; restructure minimally and keep behaviour identical when the variable is unset. Document the new env variables in the header comment (three lines).
